newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Spar expects match 1995 profit this year.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Spar expects match 1995 profit this year.

text.p: German retail group Spar Handels-AG said on Wednesday it expected to at least match 1995's net profit in 1996 after operating earnings rose 18.7 percent in the first nine months.

The company said nine month operating income rose to 59.1 million marks from 49.8 million a year earlier. Sales, excluding value added tax, rose 0.4 percent to 9.24 billion from 9.21 billion in the year-earlier period.

Spar said full-year earnings would be boosted by the sale of SPAR Bau- und Heimwerkermaerkte GmbH, but that this would be offset by one-off costs at its Bolle subsidiary and continued additional costs at its DIY stores.
"The Spar Handels-AG management board therefore expects to be able to match the good net profit of its 1995 year," it said in a statement.

Spar warned that the trend to lower turnover in the German retail sector was likely to continue in the fourth quarter of the year. But it said that it would nonetheless post a sharp increase in sales in the period due to the consolidation of the Continent supermarket chain.
It added that it expected to improve sales slightly in the full year even without the added gains from Continent.
In 1995, Spar reported a record group net profit of 74.7 million marks.
